question: In US equities and in crypto, which information available at a session's close distinguishes names that reprice +30% / +50% / +100% within the next five sessions from similar names on the same session, and can a simple detector act on it after realistic costs?
design: E1 (research/E1/protocol.json) applied unchanged except where a market differs, listed under market_differences

US.universe: US-listed common stocks in the Nasdaq Trader directory on the download day (Nasdaq, NYSE, NYSE American, Cboe, IEX); ETFs, warrants, units, rights, preferreds, notes and SPACs excluded
US.survivorship: survivor-only: names delisted before 2026-10-08 are absent. Base rates and episode counts are biased by it; detector-vs-matched-control comparisons share the bias on both sides
US.session: US regular trading day (Yahoo daily bar)
US.costs: profiles.US: per side 1.5% under $1, 0.5% $1-5, 0.15% $5-20, 0.05% above, plus SEC fee on sales; notional $5,000; entry at the next session's open

CRYPTO.universe: Binance spot USDT pairs, including delisted/halted pairs still in exchangeInfo; stablecoins, fiat and leveraged tokens excluded
CRYPTO.survivorship: includes 214 delisted/halted pairs; pairs Binance removed from exchangeInfo entirely are absent
CRYPTO.session: UTC day (00:00-24:00); the asset trades continuously
CRYPTO.costs: profiles.CRYPTO: 0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side; notional 5,000 USDT; entry at the next UTC day's open

market_differences.price_series: the source's split-adjusted close; previous = prior close (no exchange reference resets)
market_differences.price_limits: none: no ARA/ARB locks, so the binary signal ara is dropped
market_differences.matching: same session, price band, liquidity quintile; market cap is unavailable (no share or supply counts) and is therefore not matched (every name falls in the same unknown bucket)
market_differences.signals_unavailable: freqr (trade counts), turn and logmcap (share counts)
market_differences.signal_added: gap = open / previous close - 1 (opening prices exist in both sources)
market_differences.detector_family: idxsig/rules/moonshot_g.py FAMILY G1..G11, fixed before analysis

event.forward_return: R5max(t) = max over k = 1..5 of close(t+k) / close(t) - 1, on the market's session calendar
event.episode: as in E1: starts on an eligible day with R5max >= X and no session t-5..t-1 of that name with R5max >= X

eligible_if: session t lies in a research period and t+5 lies in the same period
the name traded on t (volume > 0, close > 0, previous close > 0)
at least 20 present sessions before t
at least one present session in t+1..t+5

periods.holdout_rule: sealed: the study market ends at the last validation session; one pre-registered holdout evaluation only after a detector is frozen and validated

first_100: per market, the first 100 E30 episodes of discovery in date order, ties by ticker
matched_controls: E1-MATCH-v1 with the market's price bands; 5 per event; pool = same-session eligible non-events (R5max < 0.30) of other names

detector.selection_on_discovery_only: as in E1, per market: admissible if >= 200 flagged eligible ticker-days and the Wilson 95% lower bound of E30 precision exceeds the base rate; highest lift wins, ties by larger n; none admissible = NONE
detector.freeze: the selected names are written into moonshot_g.SELECTED and committed before any validation statistic is computed
detector.validation: as in E1, plus the idxsig harness with the market profile (entry at the next open, tiered costs) over the validation window against matched and same-session random entries

decision_policy: a prospective paper BUY requires validated detection AND a validated executable plan (paper PAPER-POLICY-v2 logic)
claims: Historical research only; nothing here is prospective performance. US results are survivor-only.
